chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Burayd ibn Mu'awiyah al-'Ijli, from Abi 'Abdillah and Abi Ja'far, peace be upon them, concerning:
About a well into which a beast, a mouse, a dog, or a bird falls and dies, he said: It is removed, then buckets are drawn from the well, then drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) with it.

key_terms.الدَّابَّةُ: a beast or animal that falls into the well
key_terms.الطَّيْرُ: a bird that may fall into the well and die
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed in the ruling
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةُ: a mouse mentioned among the animals falling into the well
key_terms.الْكَلْبُ: a dog mentioned in the case under discussion
key_terms.دِلَاءٌ: buckets drawn from the well as part of the purification process
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from the well

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a well in which an animal dies according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a well into which an animal has fallen and died. It instructs that the carcass should be removed and some buckets of water drawn out, after which the water may be used for drinking and wudu (ablution).
